drvprog.evidence: holdout ranging separation -0.319 (p=0.020) but +0.160 in 2016-19, the WRONG SIGN, turning negative only from 2020. A post-COVID rate-cycle artefact.

drvprog.good_for: confirming the CURRENT regime, crisis especially
drvprog.decided_by: separation -- held sign in every sub-period
drvprog.evidence: crisis days read ~0.9 sd above everything else; range-leaning -0.538 / -0.314 / -0.648 across the three holdout sub-periods, same sign and size throughout. Holdout null p=0.020.

crisis separation +0.172 in-sample (p=0.020) flips to -0.071 on the holdout (p=0.647); sub-periods +0.112 / -0.105 / -0.139. Mechanism check technically held (JPY/CHF |sep| 0.238 vs 0.199) but the largest single pair was EURAUD, not a funding cross.

drvprog.decided_by: separation -- sign flip between halves AND sub-periods
drvprog.evidence: crisis separation -0.108 in-sample flips to +0.082 on the holdout; sub-periods +0.073 / -0.650 / +0.224. Fails both nulls (p=0.569, p=0.686). Only 10 of 28 pairs testable: AUD and CAD have a 2y but no daily 10y, NZD has neither.

trending separation -0.199 in-sample (p=0.039) holds sign on the holdout (-0.107) but fails its null there (p=0.431), and sub-periods flip: -0.122 / -0.532 / +0.150. Forward crisis lift was x1.17 in BOTH halves -- the most consistent forward number in the programme -- but fails its null in both (p=0.255, p=0.235).

drvprog.decided_by: separation -- sign flips on every reading
drvprog.evidence: All four readings flip. |4-week change| is the sharpest: ranging +0.246 in-sample (p=0.020) reverses to -0.193 on the holdout (p=0.078) -- beats its null in BOTH halves with OPPOSITE signs, which is a real magnitude attached to an unreliable sign. The declared crowded-trade cell (top decile |net| vs P(acute crisis in 20 bars)) held direction, x1.32 in-sample and x1.21 on the holdout, but fails its null in both (p=0.196, p=0.412) -- the same shape as commodities. Reaches 7 of 28 pairs, no crosses; NZD ends 2022-02-01.
Dairy (GDT auction) and coal are not free. Iron ore TIO=F IS free but only from 2010-10-14 and is scoped to AUD, which gold already covers. Recorded as untestable rather than tested badly.

pairmech.mechanism: EURUSD: The dollar leg carries global risk and rates while EUR moves on ECB policy and growth differentials, so the pair trends when those two stories diverge and ranges when they agree. It sits at rank 1 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

EURJPY: A haven leg against a large, slow bloc, so risk-off episodes move it in one direction for weeks at a time. It sits at rank 2 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

USDJPY: The dollar leg carries global risk and rates while JPY strengthens when global risk rises and carry trades unwind, so the pair trends when those two stories diverge and ranges when they agree. It sits at rank 3 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

AUDUSD: The dollar leg carries global risk and rates while AUD moves on industrial demand and global risk appetite, so the pair trends when those two stories diverge and ranges when they agree. It sits at rank 4 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

AUDNZD: Two currencies driven by the same global demand cycle, so much of the move cancels and what is left is range-bound. It sits at rank 5 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

AUDJPY: One side is bid when risk rises and the other is sold, so a single shift in global risk pushes both legs the same way at once -- the cleanest trending structure in the set. It sits at rank 6 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

USDCAD: The dollar leg carries global risk and rates while CAD moves on crude and on the US economy it borders, so the pair trends when those two stories diverge and ranges when they agree. It sits at rank 7 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

NZDJPY: One side is bid when risk rises and the other is sold, so a single shift in global risk pushes both legs the same way at once -- the cleanest trending structure in the set. It sits at rank 8 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

GBPUSD: The dollar leg carries global risk and rates while GBP moves on UK policy and its own politics, so the pair trends when those two stories diverge and ranges when they agree. It sits at rank 9 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

GBPJPY: A haven leg against a mid-sized open economy, so risk-off episodes move it in one direction for weeks at a time. It sits at rank 10 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

CADJPY: One side is bid when risk rises and the other is sold, so a single shift in global risk pushes both legs the same way at once -- the cleanest trending structure in the set. It sits at rank 11 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

NZDCAD: Two currencies driven by the same global demand cycle, so much of the move cancels and what is left is range-bound. It sits at rank 12 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

CHFJPY: Both are bid when risk rises, so they largely offset and the pair moves on the difference between two central banks. It sits at rank 13 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

AUDCHF: One side is bid when risk rises and the other is sold, so a single shift in global risk pushes both legs the same way at once -- the cleanest trending structure in the set. It sits at rank 14 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

GBPAUD: A mid-sized open economy against a commodity and China-growth proxy, so it moves on the gap between two policy cycles. It sits at rank 15 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

NZDUSD: The dollar leg carries global risk and rates while NZD moves on soft commodities and global risk appetite, with the thinnest liquidity of the eight, so the pair trends when those two stories diverge and ranges when they agree. It sits at rank 16 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

USDCHF: The dollar leg carries global risk and rates while CHF strengthens when European risk rises, and is periodically managed by its central bank, so the pair trends when those two stories diverge and ranges when they agree. It sits at rank 17 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

EURNZD: A large, slow bloc against a small commodity currency, so it moves on the gap between two policy cycles. It sits at rank 18 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

AUDCAD: Two currencies driven by the same global demand cycle, so much of the move cancels and what is left is range-bound. It sits at rank 19 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

EURCAD: A large, slow bloc against an oil-linked North American currency, so it moves on the gap between two policy cycles. It sits at rank 20 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

EURCHF: A haven leg against a large, slow bloc, so risk-off episodes move it in one direction for weeks at a time. It sits at rank 21 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

NZDCHF: One side is bid when risk rises and the other is sold, so a single shift in global risk pushes both legs the same way at once -- the cleanest trending structure in the set. It sits at rank 22 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

EURAUD: A large, slow bloc against a commodity and China-growth proxy, so it moves on the gap between two policy cycles. It sits at rank 23 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

GBPNZD: A mid-sized open economy against a small commodity currency, so it moves on the gap between two policy cycles. It sits at rank 24 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

EURGBP: Two neighbouring economies on similar policy paths, so the two legs mostly cancel and the pair spends its time going nowhere. It sits at rank 25 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

CADCHF: One side is bid when risk rises and the other is sold, so a single shift in global risk pushes both legs the same way at once -- the cleanest trending structure in the set. It sits at rank 26 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

GBPCHF: A haven leg against a mid-sized open economy, so risk-off episodes move it in one direction for weeks at a time. It sits at rank 27 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

GBPCAD: A mid-sized open economy against an oil-linked North American currency, so it moves on the gap between two policy cycles. It sits at rank 28 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

chronep.what_happened: BoJ announces Quantitative and Qualitative Easing under Kuroda: monetary base to double in two years. Ends when Kuroda tells the Diet (2015-06-10) the real effective rate is unlikely to fall further.

BoJ reaffirms unlimited fixed-rate JGB purchases to defend yield curve control while the Fed and ECB tighten -- the explicit divergence decision. Ends when the BoJ raises its policy rate to 0.25% and announces taper.
chronep.source_type: BoJ policy statement; MoF intervention record

chronep.what_happened: ECB cuts the deposit rate below zero for the first time; extended by the 2015-01-22 QE announcement. Ends when asset purchases actually begin.
Fed ends QE3 asset purchases, formalising the divergence with the ECB and BoJ. SAME MACRO EVENT as the EUR row above, seen from the other side.
SNB signals it will no longer act decisively against appreciation, and the franc is bid as a haven through the euro-area sovereign crisis. Ends the day the SNB imposes the 1.20 floor.
chronep.source_type: SNB policy statements; SNB floor announcement

chronep.what_happened: EU referendum result announced. Kept because the drift continued for months on policy expectations, but flagged: this one begins with a shock, so it is part acute and is the least clean member of this list.
chronep.source_type: Referendum result; BoE August 2016 stimulus package
